newsitem.title: UK: Rolls-Royce to strip down to aerospace - paper.
newsitem.headline: Rolls-Royce to strip down to aerospace - paper.

text.p: Rolls-Royce Plc is planning a reorganisation which will involve selling many of its remaining industrial power operations and its materials-handling business, according to the Sunday Times newspaper.
The newspaper said chief executive John Rose wanted to focus resources on the company's aerospace operations and on its aero-derived industrial power business.
Its marine-engine and specialised nuclear business will also be a key focus, the paper said.

Rolls-Royce was preparing to issue 90-day protective redundancy notices to all 1,700 staff at its Parson's steam turbine factory in Newcastle, which will close next year unless a buyer is found, the Sunday Times said.
The paper said Rolls and Siemens were in discussions to link their switchgear and transformer activities to create a venture with sales of more than 1.0 billion stg.
It said a joint-venture had been considered, but Siemens favours an outright purchase of the Rolls-Royce businesses, Reyrolle on Tyneside and Peebles near Edinburgh.
A disposal of these businesses could net 150 million stg for Rolls-Royce.
The divestment could also include Rolls' Clarke Chapman cranes and heavy lift business.

Parsons and International Combustion, the boiler making subsidiary which is scheduled to be sold or closed, could be sold to Siemens, the paper said. It already carries out some subcontract work for Siemens.
A spokesman for Rolls-Royce said the company had no comment on the report, which he said was "speculation."
"We do not have a strategy of getting rid of everything except gas turbines," he said. "We have previously stated that we will focus on companies where we have a leading market position."
He said Reyrolle and Peebles both make products which have such a position.
